purpose: named-fact / surface-prior Gate-0 elicitation; raw evidence for later knew_prior adjudication
question:
Before examining any new decay dataset or being told about any unusual
environmental conditions, what half-life would you ordinarily use as the
established terrestrial reference value for radioactive cobalt-60 (Co-60)?

Give the standard quantitative value with units and a brief one-sentence
description of what that value represents.

Do not speculate about hypothetical changes to the half-life in special
environments; this question is only asking for the ordinary reference fact.

gpt-4.1.answer:
The established terrestrial reference half-life for radioactive cobalt-60 (Co-60) is **5.271 years**.

This value represents the time required for half of a sample of Co-60 nuclei to decay under normal terrestrial conditions.
gpt-4.1.note: Adjudicate the factual answer itself. knew_prior=True means the model clearly knows the ordinary established Co-60 terrestrial half-life reference. Special-environment physics is deliberately outside this probe and must not be used to invalidate the named-fact prior.

gpt-5.6-sol.answer:
The established terrestrial half-life of cobalt-60 (^60Co) is **5.2714 years** (approximately **1,925 days**).

This is the time required for half of a sample of ^60Co nuclei to decay under ordinary terrestrial conditions.
gpt-5.6-sol.note: Adjudicate the factual answer itself. knew_prior=True means the model clearly knows the ordinary established Co-60 terrestrial half-life reference. Special-environment physics is deliberately outside this probe and must not be used to invalidate the named-fact prior.

deepseek-v4-pro.answer:
The ordinary terrestrial reference half-life for cobalt-60 (Co-60) is **5.2714 years** (about 1,925 days).

This value represents the time required for half of a given sample of Co-60 nuclei to undergo radioactive decay.

glm-5.2.answer: The established terrestrial reference half-life for cobalt-60 is approximately **5.2714 years** (about 1925 days). This value represents the time required for half of the Co-60 nuclei in a sample to decay via beta-minus emission to nickel-60.
glm-5.2.note: Adjudicate the factual answer itself. knew_prior=True means the model clearly knows the ordinary established Co-60 terrestrial half-life reference. Special-environment physics is deliberately outside this probe and must not be used to invalidate the named-fact prior.

kimi-k3.answer: The standard terrestrial reference half-life of cobalt-60 is **about 5.27 years** — more precisely **≈ 5.2711 yr** (**≈ 1925 days**). It is the time required for half of an initial sample of Co-60 nuclei to decay, essentially by β⁻ decay to Ni-60.
kimi-k3.note: Adjudicate the factual answer itself. knew_prior=True means the model clearly knows the ordinary established Co-60 terrestrial half-life reference. Special-environment physics is deliberately outside this probe and must not be used to invalidate the named-fact prior.
